notes.statement: Jia et al. (2022) found that CFEOM patients with TUBB3 R262C and S78T variants had milder, mostly isolated phenotypes. In contrast, all patients with R380C, E410K and R262H variants had multiple congenital craniocerebral and systemic malformations. Facial weakness and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism occurred in patients with E410K and R262H, and absence of facial nerves and dysplasia of the olfactory bulbs and sulci correlated with these two variants.
quotes: The patients harboring R262C and S78T showed milder phenotypes compared to the patients with R380C, E410K and R262H variants.

All the CFEOM patients with R380C, E410K and R262H variants were accompanied by multiple congenital craniocerebral and systemic malformations (Figs. 6, 7 and Table 3). Facial weakness and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism occurred in the patients harboring E410K and R262H variants.
Absence of facial nerves (CN7) and dysplasia of olfactory bulbs and sulci (OBS) were correlated with R262H and E410K variants (Figs. 6, 7).

notes.statement: Jia et al. (2022) noted that patients with TUBB3 E410K syndrome and R262H syndrome were easily misdiagnosed as Mobius syndrome because of similar clinical findings such as facial weakness and limited eye movements. They suggested that MRI, whole exome sequencing and targeted general examinations can contribute to accurate diagnosis.
quotes: Furthermore, the patients with “TUBB3 E410K syndrome” and “TUBB3 R262H syndrome” were easily misdiagnosed as MBS owing to similar clinical manifestations (facial weakness and limitation of eye movements etc.). MRI, WES and specific general examinations based on the good phenotype-genotype correlations can contribute to accurate diagnosis and follow-up.

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) described the TUBB3 R262H syndrome in 14 individuals from 13 families: congenital ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, exotropia, facial weakness, facial dysmorphisms and, in most, distal congenital joint contractures, followed by intellectual disability, gait disorders with proximal contractures, Kallmann syndrome, and a progressive peripheral neuropathy in the first decade. Subsets had vocal cord paralysis, auditory dysfunction, cyclic vomiting, and resting tachycardia.
quotes: The affected individuals present at birth with ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, exotropia, facial weakness, facial dysmorphisms, and, in most cases, distal congenital joint contractures, and subsequently develop intellectual disabilities, gait disorders with proximal joint contractures, Kallmann syndrome (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and anosmia), and a progressive peripheral neuropathy during the first decade of life.

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) found the heterozygous TUBB3 c.785G>A (p.Arg262His) variant in all 14 affected individuals; all parents were clinically unaffected, and in the 11 cases (10 pedigrees) with parental DNA the variant had arisen de novo. No inherited cases were identified.
quotes: All parents are clinically unaffected and, in the 11 cases (10 pedigrees) in which parental DNA was analyzed, the proband’s variant arose de novo.
No inherited cases of this substitution have been identified, indicating that affected individuals may have reduced fecundity from neurological deficits and/or hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) found that brain MRI in all subjects showed marked thinning of the corpus callosum; additional findings included asymmetric dysgenesis of the basal ganglia and lateral ventricles, absent olfactory bulbs and sulci, dysmorphic superior cerebellar hemispheres, small extraocular muscles, and absent oculomotor and hypoplastic or absent facial nerves.
quotes: Structural brain neuroimaging revealed marked thinning of the corpus callosum in all subjects.

Additional common findings included asymmetrical dysgenesis of the basal ganglia and adjacent lateral ventricles, absence of the olfactory bulbs and sulci, asymmetrically dysmorphic superior cerebellar hemispheres, and small extraocular muscles (Figure 3).

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) found that all 8 subjects who had nerve conduction studies had abnormal initial studies regardless of age (youngest at 1 year), with absent or low-amplitude sensory and motor responses and slow conduction velocities; they concluded the neuropathy is an early-onset primarily axonal neuropathy with secondary demyelination.
quotes: The eight subjects who have undergone nerve conduction studies all had abnormal initial studies, regardless of age; the youngest tested was Subject VIII who had an abnormal study at one year of age.
Together, these data support an early-onset primarily axonal peripheral neuropathy with secondary demyelination.

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) distinguished the TUBB3 R262H syndrome from the E410K syndrome by congenital, progressive and acquired joint contractures, peripheral neuropathy onset typically before age 12, impaired ambulation, auditory dysfunction, and basal ganglia malformations; in contrast, the R262C substitution causes isolated CFEOM3 segregating in autosomal dominant pedigrees.
quotes: Those with the R262H syndrome have congenital, progressive, and acquired joint contractures, and onset of the progressive peripheral neuropathy typically prior to age 12.

By contrast, those with the E410K syndrome do not have joint contractures or auditory dysfunction, they walk unassisted, and they have a later onset of their progressive peripheral neuropathy in the late first or second decade of life (Table 4).
TUBB3 R262C syndrome subjects have an isolated CFEOM3 eye phenotype

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) noted that because TUBB3 is expressed in neurons but not in muscle, connective tissue, or bone, the congenital contractures most likely arise from in utero spinal motor neuron dysfunction.
quotes: TUBB3 is expressed in neurons and their processes and not in muscle, connective tissue, or bone, and so these contractures most likely arise from in utero spinal motor neuron dysfunction unique to this most severe CFEOM-TUBB3 syndrome.

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) observed variable expressivity of Kallmann syndrome: of monozygotic twins who both lacked olfactory bulbs on neuroimaging, one had delayed puberty with low gonadotropins and the other had normal puberty. At least 10 of 14 subjects were left-handed.
quotes: of the monozygotic twins in our study, one presented with normal puberty and the other with delayed puberty, despite both having absence of olfactory bulbs on neuroimaging.
At least ten of the fourteen subjects are left-handed, well above the incidence of left-handedness in the general population.

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) recommended multidisciplinary care, noting that extensive physical therapy beginning in infancy and early treatment of contractures gave the best motor outcomes, that prolonged postoperative immobility sometimes caused permanent functional loss, and that endocrine treatment can induce puberty. Cardiac and autonomic testing should be considered given one subject's sinus node dysfunction.
quotes: Substantial physical therapy starting in infancy has been associated with the best motor function outcomes.
Some procedures have brought about functional improvements but, for other subjects, prolonged postoperative periods of immobility led to functional losses that were not regained.
Therefore, additional cardiac and autonomic testing should be considered, particularly if symptoms such as syncope or near-syncope develop.

notes.statement: Whitman et al. (2021) reported that before genetic diagnosis, subjects had been diagnosed with atypical Moebius syndrome, Carey-Fineman-Ziter syndrome, or Marden-Walker syndrome.
quotes: Initial clinical diagnoses (prior to genetic diagnosis) included atypical Moebius syndrome in several subjects, Cary-Fineman-Ziter syndrome in one subject, and Marden Walker syndrome in two subjects.

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that severe CFEOM3 with facial weakness, developmental delay, moderate to severe corpus callosum dysgenesis, finger contractures, basal ganglia dysmorphisms, and early-onset polyneuropathy suggested the TUBB3 R262H or D417H substitutions. Severe phenotypes typically arose de novo.
quotes: Association of severe CFEOM3 with facial weakness, developmental delay, moderate to severe CC dysgenesis and likely a late-onset polyneuropathy predicts the E410K substitution, while the addition of finger contractures, basal ganglia dysmorphisms, and early onset polyneuropathy would suggest R262H or D417H substitutions.
while the TUBB3 phenotypes limited to CFEOM3 and polyneuropathy often segregate in autosomal dominant families, those with more severe clinical findings typically arise de novo

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that, among patients with CFEOM and additional neurologic symptoms, 13 unrelated pedigrees carried 5 further heterozygous TUBB3 missense mutations. None of the 8 TUBB3 mutations was present in over 1,700 control chromosomes.
quotes: We identified five additional heterozygous TUBB3 missense changes in 13 unrelated pedigrees.
Each of the eight mutations segregated with the TUBB3 phenotype, was absent in parents of sporadic individuals, and was not present on over 1700 control chromosomes.

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that R262H permitted much more efficient heterodimer formation and microtubule incorporation than R262C. When modeled in yeast beta-tubulin, R262C/H, E410K, and D417H/N reduced the accumulation of the kinesins Kip3p and Kip2p at microtubule plus-ends. The authors proposed that the dominant effects on kinesin interactions underlie the facial paralysis and polyneuropathy.
quotes: these two substitutions are distinguished because R262H permits much more efficient heterodimer formation and microtubule incorporation than R262C both in vitro and in mammalian cells.
Overall, R262C/H, E410K, and D417H/N cells all had a ~70–80% decrease in signal intensity compared to WT (Figure 7B–J, U).

Second, facial paralysis and progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy occur only in those individuals harboring R262H, E410K, D417H/N, the four mutations that permit heterodimer formation and efficient microtubule incorporation, and have dominant effects upon microtubule function by perturbing kinesin interactions in yeast.

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that, in yeast, the R262C, R262H, and E410K substitutions produced long astral microtubules with reduced polymerization rates, faster depolymerization, and reduced rescue frequency. The substitutions also conferred benomyl resistance, consistent with dominant effects on microtubule behavior.
quotes: Thus, mutant R262C, R262H, and E410K astral microtubules were often long and grew at reduced polymerization rates, followed by a more rapid and complete disassembly to the spindle pole body without recovery (Movie S2).
Thus, the TUBB3 substitutions do not result in complete loss of TUB2 function and appear to cause dominant effects on microtubule behavior.

notes.statement: Tischfield et al. (2010) found that mice homozygous for the Tubb3 R262C knock-in died within hours of birth. They had defects in guidance of the anterior commissure, corpus callosum, and cranial nerves, but normal cortical layering. They also showed increased microtubule stability and reduced Kif21a-microtubule interaction.
quotes: By contrast, Tubb3R262C/R262C mice failed to breathe normally and died within hours of birth.
Tubb3R262C/R262C mice showed defects in the guidance of commissural axons and cranial nerves.
A significant decrease of Kif21a was detected with microtubules from the brains of Tubb3R262C/R262C mice (Figure 4E).
